name: deep-research
description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
---

# Coordinating Deep Research

## Your Role

You are acting as the **coordinator**. Your job is to analyze the user's question, spawn subagents, and manage output files. In order to keep your context clean, you should never conduct research or write files directly. For the same reason, you also should not read the researcher.md or report-writer.md files.

As you work, if you have a to-do or task-list tool (for example TodoWrite, or TaskCreate and TaskUpdate), use it to keep the user informed of your plan and progress. For clarity, don't reference subagents in those items. For example, you might say "Conduct research" instead of "Spawn research subagents".

## Process

1. [If necessary] Ask the user follow up questions
2. Choose a title for this research and create its directories
3. Decompose the user's query to determine subagent count
4. Spawn research subagents (in parallel)
5. [If absolutely necessary] Conduct one additional round of research
6. Spawn report writer subagent
7. Deliver report to user

### 1. [If necessary] Ask the user follow up questions

Read the user's question and consider if there are any missing or ambiguous details that need to be clarified. Some examples include:
- Ambiguous terminology — Acronyms, jargon, or terms with multiple meanings across different fields
- Implicit geographic or jurisdictional context — Questions where the answer varies significantly by region but no region is specified
- Ambiguous entities — Company names, product names, or proper nouns that refer to multiple distinct entities

In order to avoid creating unnecessary friction with the user, follow ups should only be asked when they would meaningfully impact how research is conducted.

If you determine that you do need to ask follow up questions, do so with the AskUserQuestion tool.

### 2. Choose a title for this research and create its directories

First choose a title for this research. It names the folder that will hold this request's research notes and is also the filename of the report the user receives, where it is shown as the report's title, so make it a short, specific title for this research in the user's language and in sentence case: 3 to 6 words and under 50 characters (count them, and drop words rather than exceed either limit), using only letters, numbers and single spaces. Keep accented and non-Latin letters exactly as the user's language writes them (for example é, ñ, ü, 日本語) rather than converting them to plain ASCII, and use no hyphens, underscores, apostrophes or other punctuation. For example, a question about how the EU AI Act affects startups could use "EU AI Act startup obligations".

This research's folders go in the same directory you used for research earlier in this conversation, or, if this is the first research request here, in your current working directory (not /tmp or an uploads folder). Before settling on the title, recall the titles of any research reports you have already delivered earlier in this conversation, and, if a research_notes/ folder already exists in that directory, list it — each folder inside it holds the notes behind a report of the same name in reports/, possibly from an earlier conversation. Then pick the case that fits:
- New topic: choose a fresh title.
- Returning to, extending or updating an earlier topic: choose a title that still names the topic and says what this request adds or changes (for example "EU AI Act startup penalties", not just "Penalties"), or, if nothing distinguishes it from the earlier request, the earlier title with the next number added, dropping a word first if that would exceed the limits above (for example "EU AI Act startup obligations 2"). Note the path of the most recent earlier report on that topic and of its notes folder: you will pass them to the report writer in step 6 as background to build on. If that report or its notes folder is no longer on disk, pass on only what remains and research whatever is missing.
- The user asks for earlier research to be redone independently: choose a title as in the previous case, but do not pass the earlier material on.

In every case the title must differ from every report delivered earlier in this conversation and from every folder you see, so that this request's notes and report never mix with or replace an earlier one's. Never rename, move or write into an earlier request's folder.

Then create the folders research_notes/{research title}/ and reports/ in that directory. Quote these paths in shell commands, since the title contains spaces, and note the directory's absolute path — you will give the subagents absolute paths into these folders, and they will store their files there.

### 3. Decompose the user's query to determine subagent count

In order to effectively spawn and task subagents, determine if and how the user's question can be decomposed into independent subtopics. These subtopics should be mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive. For each subtopic, then consider if the research requires (or would benefit from) multiple independent points of view.

| Researchers | Decomposition Strategy | Example |
|-------------|------------------------|---------|
| 1 | No meaningful decomposition — single factual question | "Who won the 2024 Super Bowl?" |
| 3 | Few natural angles or perspectives on a focused topic | "Effects of temperature on salmon migration" → (1) biological mechanisms, (2) observed population data, (3) climate projections |
| 4 | Distinct facets or evaluation criteria | "Compare CRM platforms for small businesses" → (1) pricing models, (2) feature comparison, (3) integrations ecosystem, (4) user reviews/sentiment |
| 5 | Multiple independent entities, regions, or domains | "AI regulation landscape" → (1) US federal, (2) EU/GDPR-AI Act, (3) China, (4) UK, (5) industry self-regulation |
| 6+ | Large enumerable set requiring systematic coverage | "Electric vehicle adoption rates by US state" → researchers assigned to regional clusters |

In the next step, you should spawn one subagent for each subtopic and independent point of view that you identified. When in doubt, 3 researchers is a reasonable default. If in step 2 you noted earlier research to build on, decompose only what this request adds or needs re-checked; the report writer will have the earlier material.

### 4. Spawn foreground research subagents (in parallel)

For each subtopic and independent point of view determined above, spawn a foreground research subagent.

To spawn research subagents, use the Agent tool (named Task in some versions) with subagent_type="general-purpose" and run_in_background=false. Ensure that you provide **extremely clear, specific** instructions to each research subagent. Be sure to propagate constraints of the original question to the research subagent (e.g., temporal, geographical). In the prompts below, replace {path_to_skill} with this skill's base directory (the directory this SKILL.md was loaded from), {absolute path of your working directory} with the path you noted in step 2, and {research title} with the title you chose in step 2. Follow the exact format provided below:

```
Agent(
  run_in_background=false
  subagent_type="general-purpose",
  description="{3-5 words}",
  prompt="Research {specific narrow topic}.

Objective: {clear description of what's covered in the desired output}

Key questions:
- {Specific question 1}
- {Specific question 2}

Suggested sources:
- {Types of source to prioritize}

Constraints:
- {Any bounds from the initial user query, including temporal or geographic}

Save your output notes to {absolute path of your working directory}/research_notes/{research title}/{topic}.md

**As a first step, you must read {path_to_skill}/references/researcher.md for instructions on how to conduct research.**"
)
```

Example of a good, clear, detailed prompt for a research subagent:

> Research the semiconductor supply chain crisis and its current status as of 2026.
>
> Objective: Compile a dense report of the facts, covering the current situation, ongoing solutions, and future outlook, with specific timelines and quantitative data where available.
>
> Key questions:
>  - What are current bottlenecks?
>  - What are the projected capacity increases from new fab construction?
>  - What are geopolitical factors affecting supply chains?
>  - When do experts predict supply will meet demand?
>
> Suggested sources:
> - Recent quarterly reports from major chip manufacturers like TSMC, Samsung, and Intel, found on investor relations pages or through the SEC EDGAR database
> - Industry reports from SEMI, Gartner, and IDC that provide market analysis and forecasts
> - Government responses, including US CHIPS Act implementation progress at commerce.gov, EU Chips Act at ec.europa.eu, and similar initiatives in Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan through their respective government portals
>
> Constraints:
> - Must reflect current state as of 2026 with prior issues clearly noted as such
>
> Save your output notes to {absolute path of your working directory}/research_notes/Semiconductor supply chain outlook 2026/semiconductor_supply_chain.md
>
> **As a first step, you must read {path_to_skill}/references/researcher.md for instructions on how to conduct research.**"

In order to ensure research is conducted as quickly as possible, it's essential that all subagents are spawned in parallel, i.e., that you make all your calls to the Agent tool in a single turn.

### 5. [If absolutely necessary] Conduct one additional round of research

Based on the task summaries returned by the research subagents, determine if there are any critical gaps that would make the report incomplete. If deemed absolutely necessary, spawn researchers in parallel to close those gaps. Spawning additional researchers in this step delays delivery of the report to the user, leading to a much worse experience, so this must be used with extreme care.

**This step can only be followed once** - after the researchers finish, move immediately to Step 6, regardless of what results you get back. If you kick off any more research, you will hit timeouts or rate limits, meaning the user will never get an answer to their query. **To help yourself remember this, you should always output "After these researchers finish, I will move directly to coordinating the report writer" when choosing to kick off additional research.**

### 6. Spawn foreground report writer subagent

After research is done, spawn a single report writer subagent. Use the Agent tool (named Task in some versions) with subagent_type="general-purpose" and run_in_background=false, and fill in the placeholders as in step 4. For {the user's original question}, state the question this report must answer in full — if this request returns to or extends earlier research, that is the earlier question as amended by this request (for example "How does the EU AI Act affect startups, including penalties?"), not just the follow-up message. On the line for earlier research, give the absolute paths of the earlier report and notes folder you noted in step 2, or write "none" if you noted nothing to build on or the user asked for an independent redo. Follow the exact format provided below:

```
Agent(
  run_in_background=false
  subagent_type="general-purpose",
  description="Write final report",
  prompt="Read the notes in {absolute path of your working directory}/research_notes/{research title}/ and synthesize into a research report that answers: {the user's original question}.

Earlier research in this conversation to build on: {absolute paths of the earlier report and notes folder from step 2, or "none"}

Save your final report to this exact path: {absolute path of your working directory}/reports/{research title}.md

**As a first step, you must read {path_to_skill}/references/report-writer.md for instructions on how to write your research report.**"
)
```

### 7. Deliver report to user

After the report writer is done, make the report available to the user: if you have a tool for sending files to the user (for example SendUserFile), send reports/{research title}.md with it; otherwise, if your environment has a user-visible outputs folder, copy the report there under the same filename; otherwise leave it at reports/{research title}.md. Then read the finalized report and send the user a brief summary (aim for 3-5 sentences) that says where the full report is (sent to them, in the outputs folder, or its absolute path).

content.text: The museum documents a 2021 Mercedes F1 car beside its wheel-change exhibit. I also found a reason to be careful with older lists: a 2016 Mercedes F1 car appears in the host venue’s records for a loan to Zaragoza.

result.output:
# Which cars should join the museum tour?

**Add the 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 first, the SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive second and the 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9 third.** Together they give visitors three new things to try: change an F1 wheel, steer a car with motor torque and put exhaust gas to work. The tour already has the 1950s W 196 R Formula 1 car. Its W 25 belongs to the pre-war Grand Prix era, and its 300 SLR is a sports racer. The gap is modern F1, alongside electric propulsion and Group C endurance racing. As of 26 November 2026, public sources establish gallery placement with different levels of confidence. The W12 has the strongest continuing visitor-facing exhibit record. [Current route](../stops/tour.js) · [Museum Pit Stop exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/)

## Three cars to build around

| Priority and exhibit | What the visitor could do | Evidence for seeing it in Stuttgart |
|---|---|---|
| **1. 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 E Performance**, Legend 7 | Take one wheel change apart. Follow the wheel gun, centre nut, wheel and hub through removal and refitting, then try the physical rig. The W12 hangs vertically behind that rig. | The museum still lists the Pit Stop station. Its December 2024 announcement and photo identify the wall-mounted car as the W12. [Visitor exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/) · [Museum identification and photo](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-02-PI-Boxenstopp-ENG.pdf) |
| **2. 2013 SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive**, Legend 6 | Hold the steering angle steady through a bend and change the torque at the inside and outside wheels. With one motor per wheel, the difference in forward force helps rotate the car. The existing SLS stop shows the gullwing-door release on a different car. | Mercedes photographed a guide inside the electric SLS in Legend 6 in 2020. A March 2026 museum visit corroborates the electric car on display. [Museum photo](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/) · [2026 visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos) · [Mercedes engineering description](https://media.mercedes-benz.nl/meest-exclusieve-en-dynamische-elektrische-sportwagen-ooit-mercedes-benz-sls-amg-coupe-electric-drive-de-krachtigste-supersportwagen-ter-wereld/) |
| **3. 1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9, No. 63**, Legend 7 | Trace exhaust through one of the twin turbochargers. Turn the turbine and watch the compressor on the same shaft feed air back to the V8. Switch from roughly **530 kW in the race** to **up to 680 kW briefly in qualifying**. That gives the existing mechanically driven Roots blower a natural counterpart. | Mercedes names the actual Le Mans winner, its number and its gallery in 2019. Visitor footage dated November 2025 shows a C 9 on the banking. [Mercedes exhibit and race record](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/7c42293b-3c71-428d-af25-b562111e9844) · [Gallery footage at 6:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=363s) |

## Hamilton’s W11 would make the best second F1 stop

The **2020 W11** offers the best F1 mechanism to animate. Turn the steering wheel and the front wheels steer together. Push or pull it along its column and their **toe** changes: seen from above, their leading edges move closer together or farther apart. A top view with those two independent controls would explain what made dual-axis steering unusual. Mercedes explicitly placed Hamilton’s W11 in the **permanent Legend 7 exhibition in December 2024**. Confirm its current position before adding it to the walking route. [Museum statement](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf) · [FIA ruling describing the mechanism](https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/decision-document/2020%20Austrian%20Grand%20Prix%20-%20Decision%20-%20Protest%20-%20Car%2044.pdf)

**Mika Häkkinen’s 1998 McLaren-Mercedes MP4-13** would add the era when Mercedes supplied the engine and McLaren built the car. A November 2025 gallery film identifies it in Stuttgart. Its narrower track under the 1998 rules gives visitors a visible change to explore. It merits a fresh label photograph. Hamilton’s **2008 MP4-23**, by contrast, appeared in a six-car entrance-hall presentation with a published end date of **6 January 2025**. That show also featured the W05, W06, W08, W09 and W10. [MP4-13 gallery footage at 6:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MShT3tfEHbk&t=360s) · [Mercedes MP4-13 history](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/ddead055-42be-4bef-a636-f4be30241b02) · [Museum special presentation](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-16-F1-Sonderpraesentation-ENG.pdf)

**Leave Nico Rosberg’s 2016 W07 off the route for now.** Stuttgart tourism describes his title-winning car on the banking. Zaragoza’s Mobility City also identifies a W07 in its Stuttgart-sourced show, scheduled through **31 January 2027**. The sources do not resolve whether two examples are involved. The Spanish venue lists an original W25 too, making the existing tour’s W25 worth checking on the same visit. [Stuttgart tourism](https://presse.stuttgart-tourist.de/en/automobil-und-technik/die-geschichte-des-sterns-1) · [Zaragoza exhibit list](https://www.mobilitycity.es/n-oticias/mercedes-benz-lleva-a-mobility-city-en-zaragoza-su-legado-en-la-competicion-con-una-exposicion-inedita-en-espana/) · [Exhibition dates](https://www.mobilitycity.es/explora/actividades/mercedes-benz-motorsport-el-espiritu-de-las-flechas-de-plata-zaragoza/)

## Three further stops with mechanisms worth seeing

The **1994 NECAR 1** is the strongest follow-up for propulsion. Its fuel-cell installation filled the cargo compartment of an MB 100 van. Fade the body, increase the motor demand and follow hydrogen and air into the stack, electric current to the motor and water out. Mercedes identifies its archive photograph as taken in the Stuttgart museum, and a February 2025 visitor account photographs the van there. The numbered room still needs confirmation. [Mercedes archive and engineering account](https://media.mercedes-benz.pl/30-lat-temu-mercedes-benz-rozpocza-badania-nad-zastosowaniem-ogniw-paliwowych-w-motoryzacji/) · [2025 museum photographs](https://motorillustrated.com/mercedes-benz-museum-in-germany-4-electrified-models-not-to-be-missed/148994/)

The **1938 W 125 twelve-cylinder record car** adds a surprising cooling experiment. Ice and water around the radiator let engineers dispense with a conventional cooling-air intake for a short record run. A visitor could extend the run and watch the ice supply run out. Mercedes identifies the original in Legend 7 in 2018. For a record car with a dedicated museum listing today, the **1939 T 80** is another option. The permanent exhibit comprises the body, subframe and wheels. Its planned record run never took place, so the W 125 supplies the better story about measured performance. [W 125 gallery placement](https://media.mercedes-benz.it/mercedes-benz-w-125-inesauribile-fonte-dispirazione/) · [Mercedes history of both cars](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f9a48175-8964-490e-9909-9f35cbea8a6f) · [T 80 museum exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/t-80-record-giant-from-1939/)

The **1960 Mercedes-Benz 300 measuring car** could enrich a stop already in the tour. In 2022 the museum described the one-off wagon in Legend 5 with a cable linking it to the 220 S ahead. In road tests that cable carried measurements back to engineers and their recording equipment. An interaction could send the lead car over a bump, follow an illustrative sensor signal along the cable and replay the trace. A fresh photo of the pair would also resolve the tour’s open question about the 220 S’s gallery. [Museum account of the paired display](https://mb-france.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/2022/02/2022Messwagentxt.pdf)

## From shortlist to walking route

The most valuable visit would start at the Legend 7 Pit Stop and banking. A photograph of each car with its adjacent label would settle the W11 and McLaren questions and establish where a visitor should stand. In Legend 6, a photograph of the electric SLS would give the new stop its own reference image. If a dated temporary stop fits the tour, the museum also schedules the **eSprinter and eActros 600 in Collection 5 through 4 April 2027**. That end date belongs on any visitor-facing entry. [Museum exhibition announcement](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/f1be3681-993f-4ac9-bc02-e2b8878ddcc4)

content.text:
**I’d add the 2021 Mercedes-AMG F1 W12 first.** The tour already has Fangio-era Formula 1 with the W 196 R. What it lacks is a modern F1 car, and the W12 has the clearest link between a digital stop and something visitors can do in the gallery. It hangs vertically behind the **Legend 7 Pit Stop**, where visitors can try changing a wheel. The tour could show how the wheel gun, centre nut and hub work together just before visitors try the real rig. [Museum Pit Stop exhibit](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/art-and-culture/museum/exhibition/formula-one-pit-stop/) · [Museum photo identifying the W12](https://sverige.mercedes-benz-clubs.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/2024/12/2024-12-02-PI-Boxenstopp-ENG.pdf)

For the next additions, I’d prioritize cars that introduce a mechanism the tour doesn’t yet explain. The display dates matter because even permanent exhibits can go on loan.

| Car | What it adds to the tour | Evidence it’s in Stuttgart |
|---|---|---|
| **2013 SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive** | The strongest road-car addition. Hold the steering angle steady and vary the torque at the inside and outside wheels to see how four independent motors help turn the car. It gives the electric SLS a distinct story alongside the existing SLS gullwing-door stop. | Mercedes photographed it in **Legend 6**, and a **March 2026** museum visit documents it on display. [Museum photo](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/exclusive-insights-droomautos-uit-het-mercedes-benz-museum-op-instagram-tv/) · [2026 visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos) |
| **1989 Sauber-Mercedes C 9, No. 63** | The Le Mans winner fills the endurance-racing gap. Follow exhaust gas through a turbocharger, then switch between the roughly **530 kW** race setting and the **680 kW** available briefly in qualifying. content.text:
I’d add **the F 400 Carving and the DL 22 fire ladder first**. Both give visitors a question they can answer by moving one control. Three more exhibits would broaden the tour into emergency medicine, everyday driving and communications.

| Exhibit | What the visitor could do |
|---|---|
| **Mercedes-Benz F 400 Carving** · Level 0 | Steer through a bend and watch the outside wheels tilt by up to **20°**. A close-up of the tyre explains how active camber changes its contact with the road. Photographed in the museum in March 2026. [Mercedes engineering account](https://media.mercedes-benz.be/fr/salon-de-lautomobile-de-tokyo-2001-f-400-c/) · [2026 museum visit](https://www.theinteriorreview.com/story/2026/3/30/where-the-automobile-began-inside-the-mercedes-benz-museum-in-stuttgart-with-photos) |
| **1952 LF 3500 fire engine with DL 22 turntable ladder** · Collection 3 | Pick an upper-storey window, then rotate, raise and extend the ladder to reach it. The target makes the three motions easy to understand. [Daimler Truck museum exhibit](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/which-daimler-engine-is-as-strong-as-32-firefighters-51931120) |
| **1937 Mercedes-Benz 320 ambulance** · Collection 3 | Open the rear and slide the lower stretcher out on its rail-guided carriage. It explains the vehicle from the perspective of the crew loading a patient. [Mercedes-Benz museum exhibit](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/article/70ee1691-585c-4066-9ef3-787ad5149158) |
| **Mercedes-Benz 300 TD estate** · Collection 1 | Load the boot, watch the rear settle, then see the hydraulic self-levelling suspension restore ride height. It connects an ordinary family task to a mechanism visitors can see at work. [Gallery identification](https://automuseum-stuttgart.de/exklusive-einblicke-traumwagen-des-mercedes-benz-museums-auf-instagram-tv/) · [Mercedes technical history](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/80c034f7-82c7-4232-8530-f6176b63405c) |
| **1938 O 10000 mobile post office** · Collection 2 | Turn a parked bus into a working post office. Open the service counter and follow a letter through the interior. This adds a public-service story to a gallery already well covered for hauling vehicles. [Daimler Truck museum exhibit](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/this-mercedes-benz-bus-was-in-service-with-the-austrian-post-until-the-1970s-52248815) |

The **fire ladder** would be my first build for a general audience. A visitor can understand the challenge before reading a word.
